You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I failed because I entered a loop between the Craft room, Exercise room, Bathroom, and Attic without realizing I had already visited all unique rooms. I kept moving until I returned to the start, assuming unvisited rooms remained, but I never checked the set of visited nodes against the total count of unique rooms found. Next time, after every move, I will explicitly count the unique nodes in my `graph["nodes"]` list. If the count of unique nodes equals the number of times I have been told "You have made a step and entered [Room Name]" (excluding the start), I will immediately output "DONE" instead of taking another step, ensuring I stop exactly when the map is fully explored.

New plan: I failed because I stopped at the Bathroom after returning from the Exercise room, assuming the map was complete, but I never verified if all reachable rooms had been visited. I also failed to update the `edges` dictionary correctly; I kept the old edges and did not add the new connection between the Exercise room and the Craft room. Next time, after every move, I will explicitly add the new edge to the `edges` dictionary corresponding to the direction I just traveled (e.g., if I go east from Exercise to Craft, I must add `("Exercise room", "Craft room")` to `edges["east"]`). Furthermore, before outputting "DONE", I will check if the number of unique nodes in my graph matches the total number of rooms I have been told I entered. If the count is lower, I will continue exploring unvisited directions rather than stopping prematurely.
